OVV.market_view: price_implies: roughly flat to declining revenue from the TTM level at a mid-teens operating margin; EV near 22B against about 2.5B of TTM free cash flow is an 11% yield typical of a depleting E&P | where_i_differ: little: my base case holds revenue near 10B with a margin close to the 10-year median, slightly above the latest FY2025 margin, reflecting the larger Montney position and lower debt

PCRX.market_view: price_implies: about 1.46B market cap with net cash roughly zero, about 8-9 times TTM FCF of 169M: the price assumes cash flow holds near today's level for a few years and then shrinks after generic Exparel arrives around 2030 | where_i_differ: my base case is close to the market; I give more weight to GAAP margin recovery as acquisition amortization and impairment charges fade, and assume the volume-limited generic settlement slows rather than collapses Exparel revenue

PEB.market_view: price_implies: price nearly doubled off the 52-week low; at 2.41B equity it assumes AFFO margin recovering to about 10-11% with low single-digit revenue growth, roughly my base to bull | where_i_differ: my base is close to the market; I weight the high leverage and flat four-year revenue more, so I see recovery as slower and margin capped near 10%

PGR.market_view: price_implies: at about 4.0x book and 11.8x TTM earnings, the price assumes ROE fades from the mid-30s to the low 20s and stays there for a decade, with modest growth | where_i_differ: broadly in line; I give more weight to the soft-cycle margin squeeze in the next two years and to a long-run risk to personal-auto premium volume, so near-term ROE sits below the price's implied path

PNRG.market_view: price_implies: roughly flat production and revenue near 180M with a mid-cycle margin in the high teens, i.e. earnings around the TTM level sustained | where_i_differ: little in the base case; I weight the downside more because reinvestment below depletion implies volume decline unless drilling resumes

PRCH.market_view: price_implies: an enterprise value near 2.8B, about 5.7x TTM revenue and roughly 24x FCF, which assumes mid-to-high-teens growth for several years and operating margin rising toward the high teens | where_i_differ: my base case is close to the price; I weight the risk that the reciprocal's catastrophe exposure and the 404M debt load can interrupt the fee growth more than a smooth extrapolation of the last four quarters does

PSA.market_view: price_implies: at 332.59 and roughly 15 USD of AFFO per share the price is about 22x AFFO, which assumes AFFO grows about 3-4% a year for a long time at a stable margin | where_i_differ: little: my base case is close to that, with a one-off acquisition lift in year 1 and organic growth near 3.5-4%; the risk is that rent growth stays as weak as 2024-2025

PTCT.market_view: price_implies: roughly flat to low single-digit growth from the current run-rate with operating margin staying in the mid-teens, i.e. a Sephience plateau and legacy erosion | where_i_differ: base case expects Sephience to keep growing for several years and costs to scale slower than revenue; tempered by the off-sheet royalty liability (non-cash interest drives TTM net loss of -106M despite 147.7M operating income), which caps how much reported margin reaches shareholders

PYPL.market_view: price_implies: market cap of 49B against 6.3B TTM free cash flow (about a 13% yield) implies flat to declining revenue and margins eroding toward the mid-teens | where_i_differ: base case assumes the 2026 slowdown and reinvestment are a reset rather than a structural decline: mid-single-digit growth and margin recovering toward 18%, with heavy buybacks (share count down from 1,187M to 858M) supporting per-share value

R.market_view: price_implies: at about 21x TTM earnings and roughly 22x after-tax EBIT on enterprise value, the price assumes the 2026 recovery continues with mid-single-digit growth and margin rising toward 10% | where_i_differ: my base keeps margin near 9%, close to the six-year record, because the 2023-2025 used-truck and rental softness shows how cyclical the earnings are; returns on the heavy fleet capital are only modestly above cost

RCEL.market_view: price_implies: roughly 25-30% growth for several years with operating breakeven within about a year and mid-teens margins at maturity, after a near-fivefold rally from the 52-week low | where_i_differ: my base is close to that; I give more weight than the price seems to to the balance sheet, since 10.5M cash and 45.5M debt leave little room if the Q3 ramp stalls

RHP.market_view: price_implies: about 4-5% revenue growth with AFFO margin steady near 17-18% and expansion capital earning high single-digit returns, near the top of the 52-week range | where_i_differ: base case is broadly in line; I put more weight on group-demand cyclicality and leverage, held in the bear and tail cases, and on NCI taking part of Opry Entertainment profits

RLJ.market_view: price_implies: roughly 16x trailing free cash flow after capex and SBC: low single-digit revenue growth with the AFFO margin holding near 9-10%, after a rally from 7.15 to near the 52-week high | where_i_differ: little: my base sees modest RevPAR growth and slight margin recovery, but cost inflation and floating-rate refinancing cap upside, so I sit close to the market

RNG.market_view: price_implies: enterprise value near 7.2B, about 17 times FCF after SBC of roughly 430M, which fits mid-single-digit growth with GAAP margin climbing into the low-to-mid teens | where_i_differ: base case broadly matches; I see SBC decline as the main margin lever and put more weight than the price on seat erosion from AI and bundled competitors via the tail

SAH.market_view: price_implies: at about 9 times trailing earnings and a near-halving from the 52-week high, roughly flat revenue and an operating margin fading toward 2.3-2.5% after floor-plan interest | where_i_differ: I expect margins to hold near 2.8% after floor-plan cost as parts and service and franchised dealerships stay resilient; the market is pricing something closer to my bear case

SGU.market_view: price_implies: a slowly shrinking business earning roughly its ten-year median margin of about 4-5%, with the cold-winter FY2025 and TTM profits treated as non-recurring | where_i_differ: base case assumes acquisitions and margin per gallon offset volume attrition so through-cycle margin sits near 5.5%, somewhat above the long median, given rising gross profit FY2023-FY2025

SLDE.market_view: price_implies: about 2.3x book and 5x trailing earnings, i.e. ROE falling from roughly 50% to the mid-to-high teens with a meaningful catastrophe discount | where_i_differ: broadly agree; my base keeps ROE above 20% for two years before fading, because the growth and post-reform loss environment on the sheet look durable short term, but catastrophe risk caps the upside

SN.market_view: price_implies: about 38x TTM earnings: low-to-mid teens growth for years with margin rising toward 17-18% | where_i_differ: base case is close to the price; growth fades faster than the recent 20% pace because appliance categories mature and tariffs weigh on cost

SPG.market_view: price_implies: roughly 18 times FFO, an AFFO yield near 5%, consistent with 3-4% long-run growth at a stable margin, close to the record | where_i_differ: my base case is broadly in line with the market; I see the 2026 growth spike as consolidation, not organic, and expect growth to settle near 3%

SPH.market_view: price_implies: roughly flat to slightly declining revenue at a 13-14% margin with heavy distribution payout and little value for growth investments | where_i_differ: little difference: base case keeps the 14.5% normal-weather margin and about 1.5% growth from pricing and tuck-ins, slightly above a no-growth view

SSD.market_view: price_implies: an enterprise value near 7.8B, about 21 times after-tax operating income, which assumes the TTM 20% margin roughly holds with mid-to-high single digit growth | where_i_differ: I normalise margin to 19% rather than the TTM 20.5% because housing is cyclical and recent margin sits above the 10-year median; growth is similar to what the price assumes

STGW.market_view: price_implies: an equity value near 2.8B and EV near 4.3B including leases, about 11x TTM free cash flow, consistent with low single-digit growth and GAAP margin staying in the 4-6% band | where_i_differ: my base lets GAAP margin climb toward 7% as amortization of acquired intangibles fades and growth stays mid-single-digit; the 2025 exchange of noncontrolling units into class A shares means the 67.64% historic NCI share of profit no longer applies to the diluted 251M shares

STRW.market_view: price_implies: Roughly 9x AFFO on all operating-partnership units, consistent with low single-digit growth and a flat AFFO margin near 0.45, with a discount for leverage and tenant concentration | where_i_differ: Close to the market; my base allows modest acquisition-led growth above escalators, but the flat 2026 quarters, the Q3 loss and high leverage keep me from going further

STT.market_view: price_implies: at about 1.6x book the price assumes ROE holding around 12-13% with steady capital return, i.e. the recent earnings step-up largely persists | where_i_differ: broadly in line; I give equal weight to a reversion toward the 10% history as rates fall, so I do not extrapolate the 2026 peak quarters

SWBI.market_view: price_implies: revenue near the TTM 551M growing low single digits at a through-the-cycle operating margin around 8-9%, i.e. a partial recovery toward the historic median | where_i_differ: broadly in line; I see margin recovery to about 9% as the base, with upside if the recent 17-32% quarterly revenue growth persists, but firearm demand is cyclical and the 2021 surge margins are not repeatable

TASK.market_view: price_implies: roughly flat-to-low growth with margin settling near 9-10%, i.e. the market prices meaningful AI displacement of the core outsourcing book | where_i_differ: my base keeps the current 5% growth and 11% margin, since revenue still grew every quarter and the AI-services line offsets some displacement; the tail scenario carries the disruption risk explicitly

TGTX.market_view: price_implies: an EV near 10B, about 11x TTM sales: revenue rising to roughly 2B within five years at a margin near 40% | where_i_differ: my base case is close to the price; I weight more heavily the deceleration already visible in quarterly growth and single-product concentration against competing subcutaneous anti-CD20s

TLN.market_view: price_implies: an enterprise value near 25.6B (16.4B equity plus about 9.2B net debt), which needs EBIT margins near 28-30% on a revenue base that keeps growing after the acquisitions are absorbed | where_i_differ: I largely agree on margins once the one-off stock comp and hedge marks fall away, but weight a merchant price reversal and the leverage taken on for the gas acquisitions more heavily

TOP.market_view: price_implies: a market cap of about 2.1B against 117M parent equity, about 18x book, which needs a sustained ROE far above anything the firm has earned and revenue growth of many multiples from 5.1M TTM | where_i_differ: a small Hong Kong broker with shrinking revenue and a fresh, much larger equity base is unlikely to earn more than a high single digit ROE; the 95% volatility and 3 to 17 range point to trading flows, not fundamentals

TPC.market_view: price_implies: enterprise value near 4.5B, about 17x TTM after-tax operating income, which assumes the recovery holds: mid-to-high single-digit growth and margins of roughly 6-7% sustained | where_i_differ: my base broadly agrees on the backlog-driven growth but I weight a real chance of renewed project charges, given the FY2022-FY2024 losses, which the price does not appear to discount

TRMD.market_view: price_implies: near the top of the 52-week range, the price assumes rates stay firm for a few years, with margins around the high 20s rather than a fall to a 15-20% through-cycle level | where_i_differ: my base case allows a strong 2026 but fades margins to about 22% as newbuild deliveries arrive; I weight a trough more than the price appears to, given the FY2021 history

TRN.market_view: price_implies: at 2.39B market cap against 1.13B equity, about 2.1x book, the price assumes a mid-teens ROE on recurring leasing earnings that is sustained but not much higher, with little credit for the TTM gains | where_i_differ: broadly in line: I treat the TTM 30% ROE as inflated by portfolio-sale gains and noncontrolling partners taking about 11% of profit, and anchor the base on roughly 16% recurring ROE from the leasing fleet with a slow fade

TTAM.market_view: price_implies: at about 6x trailing EBITDA the price assumes revenue shrinking or flat and operating margin falling to about 11-12%, well below the 16% of FY2025 | where_i_differ: I expect a soft 2026 but a through-the-cycle margin near the 15% ten-year median, supported by integrated plants and terminals in growing Sunbelt markets and a balance sheet with low net debt

TWFG.market_view: price_implies: Counting all Class A, B and C units the whole firm is worth roughly 1.4-1.5B less about 78M cash, near 25x TTM operating income: the price assumes double-digit growth for several years and margins at or above the current 17% | where_i_differ: Little difference in the base case; I put more weight on the slowdown in the latest quarter and a softer P&C pricing cycle than a growth multiple implies, and the listed Class A holds only a minority of the economics

UGI.market_view: price_implies: enterprise value around 16x after-tax operating income: roughly 2% growth with margin held near 15% and utility-like returns on new capital | where_i_differ: my base case is close to the market; I see little room above it given heavy capex, low sales-to-capital and a propane business in structural volume decline

UVE.market_view: price_implies: about 2.1 times book and under 6 times trailing earnings: the market assumes the 2025-2026 ROE near 40% is largely weather luck and returns fade to the mid-to-high teens | where_i_differ: broadly agree; the base case also fades to mid-teens, while the tail scenario reflects that one bad Florida season can erase a year or more of earnings

VSNT.market_view: price_implies: about 4.9B equity plus about 1.9B net debt is roughly 4x TTM free cash flow of 1.64B, which assumes revenue declines of 8-10% a year for ever with margin falling toward 10% | where_i_differ: I expect a slower decline of about 4% a year with margin held in the mid-teens, since cord-cutting has run at a steady mid-single-digit pace and the company is cutting costs as a standalone; I weight a faster decline with real probability

VSXY.market_view: price_implies: at about 8.9B of enterprise value before leases, roughly 16 times TTM operating income: the price assumes the 2026 recovery holds, with mid-single-digit growth and margin rising from 7.9% toward 10% or more | where_i_differ: my base case keeps margin near 9%, below the FY2022 peak, because the sheet shows only two strong quarters after four weak years and the Q2 2026 gross-margin jump may not repeat; I give real weight to a fade back toward the 4-5% margins of FY2024-FY2026

WLY.market_view: price_implies: with about 1.3B of debt the enterprise trades near 16 times TTM free cash flow, roughly 2% growth at a flat 15-16% GAAP operating margin | where_i_differ: close to the market: I give modest margin expansion as restructuring and portfolio pruning end, offset by a real AI and open-access tail risk to journal pricing

WNC.market_view: price_implies: equity near 470M plus about 500M of net debt values the business near 0.65x trailing revenue, consistent with a recovery to roughly 4-5% through-cycle margins with modest growth | where_i_differ: base case sees a fuller cyclical recovery to about a 6% margin, in line with the ten-year median, but the leverage and current cash burn justify a material tail weight

WTM.market_view: price_implies: market cap of 5.38B against 5.35B parent equity, about 1.0x book, which implies a return on equity close to the cost of equity with little value from reinvestment | where_i_differ: little difference: base case ROE of about 9% is near what one times book implies; the long record of compounding book per share and buybacks below book gives modest upside rather than a large gap

XHR.market_view: price_implies: near the 52-week high, the price assumes steady low-single-digit revenue growth with AFFO margin holding around 11-12% and no lodging downturn | where_i_differ: my base case is close to the market; I give more weight to a cyclical lodging downturn given leverage of about 1.2B net debt against a thin GAAP margin, so the downside cases carry real probability

ZIM.market_view: price_implies: price near the 52-week high and below book equity of 4.02B suggests the market expects mid-single-digit through-the-cycle margins on revenue around 5-6B, plus some value from take-private interest | where_i_differ: little: my base sees a weak 2026-2027 as new capacity lands and Suez routing normalises, then about 7% margins; any takeover premium is not in my operating paths
